🍑 When to plant african star apple in Nigeria

Also called Agbalumo (Yoruba) and Udara (Igbo).

Quick answer: Plant african star apple in Nigeria from June to July and harvest from December to March. Planted in the rains; fruits fall in the dry season (December–March).

PlantJune to July
HarvestDecember to March

About african star apple

Agbalumo season is a much-loved dry-season treat across southern Nigeria.

How to plant african star apple well

Collect fallen fruits daily.

Planted in the rains; fruits fall in the dry season (December–March).

Diseases and pests of african star apple

  • Fruit rotPick up fallen fruits quickly.
  • Few serious diseasesKeep the area under the tree clean.

Questions farmers ask

When is the best time to plant african star apple in Nigeria?

Plant african star apple in Nigeria from June to July and harvest from December to March. Planted in the rains; fruits fall in the dry season (December–March).

What is african star apple called in Yoruba, Hausa and Igbo?

African star apple is called Agbalumo (Yoruba) and Udara (Igbo).

When is african star apple harvested in Nigeria?

African star apple is usually harvested from December to March.

Which Nigerian states grow the most african star apple?

Oyo, Ogun, Osun, Ondo, Ekiti, Edo, Enugu, Anambra and Imo are among the best-known african star apple states.

Can I grow african star apple in my part of Nigeria?

African star apple grows best in the South-West, South-East and South-South regions. In other regions, ask your ADP extension officer before planting.

What diseases attack african star apple and how do I prevent them?

Fruit rot: Pick up fallen fruits quickly. Few serious diseases: Keep the area under the tree clean.
